ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the right angle of the set square $DEF$ is placed inside $\triangle ABC$, where the two right-angle sides of the set square pass through points B and C, respectively. If $\angle A=55^\circ$, what is the sum of $\angle ABD+\angle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=55^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC+\angle ACB=180^\circ-\angle A=125^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle DBC$, $\because \angle BDC=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle DBC+\angle DCB=180^\circ-\angle BDC=90^\circ$, \\
$\angle ABD+\angle ACD=\angle ABC+\angle ACB-(\angle DBC+\angle DCB)=125^\circ-90^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ}$.
